parts.role: Runs the firmware and supplies 3.3 V from its USB-powered regulator.

nets.name: +3V3
nets.why: One 3.3 V supply from the ESP32 board’s regulator. Every part here runs at 3.3 V, so its signals match the ESP32’s 3.3 V logic.

nets.name: GND
nets.why: Common ground. Every signal is measured against it, so every part must share it.

nets.name: I2C_SCL
nets.why: I²C clock, driven by the ESP32. GPIO22 is the default SCL pin of the ESP32 Arduino Wire library. Most breakouts already carry pull-up resistors. Both I²C devices share these two wires; they answer to different addresses (OLED 0x3C, BME280 0x76).

nets.name: I2C_SDA
nets.why: I²C data, in both directions. GPIO21 is the default SDA pin of the ESP32 Arduino Wire library. Both I²C devices share these two wires; they answer to different addresses (OLED 0x3C, BME280 0x76).

nets.name: BUZZER
nets.why: GPIO23 toggles a tone (for example with ledcWriteTone) and the piezo clicks at that frequency. A passive piezo draws very little current, so the pin can drive it directly.

notes.text: OLED pin order differs between sellers (VCC and GND are sometimes swapped). Wire by the labels on your board.
Only the 3.3 V-only 4-pin BME280 breakout is modelled. Check that yours is not a BMP280, which has no humidity sensor.
